question: The percentage of energy loss per unit deformation from friction happening inside the rubber, which creates heat build-up in the rubber, and is measured as in terms of the temperature, is known as _____.
solution:
The correct answer is __Hysteresis.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Hysteresis__ refers to the percentage of energy loss per unit deformation due to friction inside the rubber.
 
• This phenomenon causes heat build-up in the rubber during deformation.
 
• It is commonly measured in terms of temperature increase.
 
• Hysteresis is a critical factor in applications such as tire performance and energy efficiency.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Stress-Strain Test:**

 
 
• It measures the mechanical properties of a material by applying stress and observing the resulting strain.
 
• It provides insights into elasticity, yield strength, and ultimate tensile strength.
 
 
 
• **Resilience:**
 
 
• It is the ability of a material to store and release energy elastically during deformation.
 
• High resilience indicates greater energy efficiency with minimal energy loss.
 
 
 
• **Creep:**
 
 
• It is the gradual deformation of a material under constant stress over time.
 
• Creep occurs more significantly at higher temperatures.
